# devcoach

> devcoach is a free, open-source MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that runs on your machine, next to your AI coding agent. When your agent finishes a task and a lesson is due, devcoach teaches you one short lesson on something that task touched and you don't know yet. A private knowledge map of what you already know keeps each lesson at your level.

- **When lessons come.** The pace is yours to set. By default: one lesson cue about every 10 interactions in a chat session, at most 2 lessons a day, at least 4 hours apart. Every number is a setting. Lesson cues pause while a course is in progress.
- **Which agents.** devcoach wires automatic lessons only into Claude Code (through the plugin or `devcoach install`), Gemini CLI (beta) and Codex CLI (beta; its hooks run only after you trust them), which also get the devcoach skill. Claude Desktop and other MCP agents (Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Continue, Zed) get devcoach's tools only: say "set up devcoach" once, then ask for a lesson ("teach me something from what we just did"). claude.ai web is not supported: it cannot reach a local MCP server. Every agent on one computer shares the same profile and lessons.
- **The first time.** After your first task devcoach offers to set up your profile and asks how: Automatic (recommended), Automatic (Deep), Guided, or Import backup.
- **Your data.** It lives in `~/.devcoach/`: a SQLite database (`coaching.db`), the coaching notebook (`learning-state.md`) and your course files (`courses/`). No account, no telemetry, no update check. devcoach makes one kind of network request, and only when you ask: importing a lesson from a web address. Your data leaves the machine only when you share a lesson or publish a course; as with anything in a session, what your agent reads from devcoach becomes part of its conversation with its model.
- **Free.** AGPL-3.0, free for everyone, at home or at work. No paid tier.
- **Also in the box.** A command line (`devcoach`), a web dashboard on `127.0.0.1`, lesson sharing, step-by-step courses, and an MCP server with 25 tools, 11 resources and 1 prompt.

Node.js 24 or newer is needed by the Claude Code plugin, npx and a global npm install. Homebrew, Scoop and the Windows installer install Node.js for you; the Claude Desktop extension runs on Claude Desktop's own.

## Start here

- [Home](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/): what devcoach does, what a lesson looks like in the terminal and in the desktop app, and a demo course that runs in the page.
- [Why devcoach](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/why): AI writes more of our code, so the scarce skill becomes validating what it produces; how short lessons on your own work keep it, compared with courses, docs, books and asking your agent to explain.
- [How it works](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/how-it-works): what happens around a turn of work with your agent: which agents get lessons on their own, what happens after your first task, when a lesson is due and why most turns end without one, and how its topic and depth are chosen.

## Install

The methods in the order the docs list them; the Claude Code plugin is the recommended one for Claude Code.

- [Choose your setup](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install): pick a method for your agent, and see what each agent gets (automatic lessons, the devcoach skill, the tools).
- [Claude Code plugin](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/claude-code-plugin): two commands typed in Claude Code, `/plugin marketplace add UltimaPhoenix/claude-plugins-marketplace` then `/plugin install devcoach@ultimaphoenix`. Bundles the MCP server, two hooks, the devcoach skill and five slash commands (`/devcoach:setup`, `:ui`, `:share`, `:import`, `:course`).
- [Homebrew](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/homebrew): macOS and Linux. `brew tap UltimaPhoenix/tap`, `brew trust --tap UltimaPhoenix/tap` (Homebrew 6 and later load nothing from an untrusted tap), then `brew install devcoach` brings Node.js and the `devcoach` command; `devcoach install` then connects Claude Code and Claude Desktop (skip it with the Claude Code plugin).
- [Windows](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/windows): beta, from devcoach 2.8.0. One PowerShell line (`irm https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install.ps1 | iex`) or Scoop; both bring Node.js and the `devcoach` command and connect Claude Code and Claude Desktop. With the Claude Code plugin, run `$env:DEVCOACH_SKIP_CONNECT = "1"` first so the line skips `devcoach install`. Update with `scoop update devcoach`, or by running the line again.
- [npx / npm](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/npx): `npx -y devcoach install` with nothing installed globally, or `npm install -g devcoach` then `devcoach install`; connects Claude Code and Claude Desktop.
- [Claude Desktop (beta)](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/claude-desktop): the self-signed `.mcpb` extension attached to every release (no terminal), or `devcoach install`. devcoach's tools; lessons when you ask.
- [Gemini CLI (beta)](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/gemini-cli): `devcoach install --gemini` with devcoach installed (Homebrew, Windows or npm), or `npx -y devcoach install --gemini` without it, or the Gemini extension. Two hooks cue a lesson when one is due.
- [Codex CLI (beta)](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/codex): `devcoach install --codex` with devcoach installed (Homebrew, Windows or npm), or `npx -y devcoach install --codex` without it. Its two hooks cue a lesson once you trust them.
- [Other MCP agents](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/other-agents): Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Continue, Zed or any MCP client: an MCP server entry that runs `npx -y devcoach mcp`, in the file and key each agent expects (the page has one tab per agent). devcoach's tools; lessons when you ask. MCP Registry name: `io.github.UltimaPhoenix/devcoach`.
- [claude.ai web (not supported)](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/install/claude-ai): why devcoach does not work in claude.ai in the browser, and what to use instead.

## Use devcoach

- [Coaching in your agent](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/usage/coaching): onboarding, your first lesson, the three answers under a lesson (✅ knew it, 💡 understood, ❌ couldn't follow), the coaching notebook, and how to set the pace.
- [Courses](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/usage/courses): a step-by-step path through one topic, for a lesson you couldn't follow (the coach offers one once) or whenever you ask. One local HTML document in `~/.devcoach/courses/`, taught one step per message.
- [Sharing lessons](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/usage/sharing): hand a lesson to a teammate as copyable text, a server-less link or a `.devcoach.md` file, and import theirs from the dashboard, the CLI or your agent; what travels with it and what never does.
- [Web dashboard](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/usage/web-ui): `devcoach ui` opens it on `127.0.0.1`: your knowledge map, every lesson with filters, courses, sharing, settings and backups.
- [Command line (CLI)](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/usage/cli): every `devcoach` command: lessons and the knowledge map, answers, settings, backup and restore, sharing, and `devcoach doctor` to check the wiring.

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/reference/configuration): the seven settings with their defaults and ranges, the pacing rules, the environment variables, your data in `~/.devcoach`, what a backup holds, restore and reset.
- [Privacy & security](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/reference/privacy): what devcoach reads and stores, the one network request it makes when you ask, and when your data leaves your machine.
- [MCP server reference](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/reference/mcp-server): the 25 tools, 11 resources and 1 prompt devcoach exposes over MCP.
- [License](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/reference/license): AGPL-3.0, free for everyone, at home or at work. Using devcoach never puts your own code under the AGPL. No paid tier, and no commercial licence on offer.

## Help

- [Troubleshooting](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/troubleshooting): `devcoach doctor`, what each symptom means and its fix, the known limitations, and how to uninstall cleanly.
- [FAQ](https://ultimaphoenix.github.io/dev-coach/faq): short answers on what devcoach is, when lessons come and how to change the pace, which agents it works with, where your data lives, what it costs, and how to install or remove it.
